guides/cpa-vs-enrolled-agent.html.desc: What separates a CPA, an Enrolled Agent and an unenrolled tax preparer — licensing, examinations, and who can represent you before the IRS when something goes wrong.
guides/cpa-vs-enrolled-agent.html.h1: CPA, Enrolled Agent, or preparer: who can actually do what.
guides/cpa-vs-enrolled-agent.html.sub: Three different things sit behind the word “accountant”. The difference rarely matters — until the day it matters a great deal.

blocks.html: Three different things sit behind the word “accountant”. The difference rarely matters — until the day it matters a great deal.

blocks.html: Anyone may call themselves an accountant. Nothing stops it, and plenty of competent people who prepare returns hold no licence at all. But the credentials behind the title are not interchangeable, and the difference is most visible at exactly the moment you would rather it were not: when the IRS writes to you.

blocks.html: Certified Public Accountant
blocks.text: Certified Public Accountant

blocks.html: A CPA is licensed by a state board of accountancy. Getting there means passing the Uniform CPA Examination and meeting that state's education and experience requirements; keeping it means continuing professional education and adherence to professional conduct rules, enforced by the board that issued the licence.
blocks.text: A CPA is licensed by a state board of accountancy. Getting there means passing the Uniform CPA Examination and meeting that state's education and experience requirements; keeping it means continuing professional education and adherence to professional conduct rules, enforced by the board that issued the licence.

blocks.html: The licence is broad. It covers tax, but also the parts of accounting practice — independent reporting on financial statements in particular — that an unlicensed person may not perform at all. A CPA also has unlimited rights to represent taxpayers before the IRS.

blocks.html: Enrolled Agent
blocks.text: Enrolled Agent

blocks.html: An Enrolled Agent is licensed by the United States Treasury rather than by a state. There are two routes in: passing the three-part Special Enrollment Examination, which covers individuals, businesses, and representation and procedure; or qualifying experience as a former IRS employee. Enrolled Agents must complete continuing education and are governed by Treasury Circular 230.

Enrolled Agents must complete continuing education and are governed by Treasury Circular 230.

blocks.html: The designation is narrower than a CPA licence in scope and identical to it in one respect that matters: representation. Under Circular 230, Enrolled Agents, CPAs and attorneys all hold unlimited practice rights before the IRS. Any taxpayer, any tax matter, any IRS office. The federal licence also means an Enrolled Agent is not confined to one state's clients.
